description: Helps you decide who inside the buyer will push for you. You give what your product does and the problem it solves, plus optional company name, target company type, price point and sector. You get hypotheses for the champion, the economic buyer, the technical influencer, commercial and control reviewers and daily users, warning signs of an anti champion, a path to develop the champion and what to give them. These are roles to test, not named people. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of buyer_group_analyzer when you need champion-role hypotheses from a product and problem.

company_name.description: Your company name. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

price_point.description: What you charge, with the period, in your own words (for example "$50,000 a year" or "$3,750 per month"). Format is text.

problem_solved.description: The core problem you solve. Format is text. For example, "invoice exceptions delay month-end close".

product_description.description: What your product does (1-2 sentences). Format is text. For example, "checks invoice exceptions before approval".

target_company_type.description: Type of companies you target (e.g., "mid-size fintech companies", "enterprise manufacturers"). Format is text.

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

name: impact_identify_champions
title: Identify Champions
